answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when independent audits prove coordinated deception. A new identity must lock fresh collateral before it can earn reputation or vote, so splitting one operator across a gale of accounts does not multiply its weight. Auditors can publish a cipher-committed evidence trail, while a falcon watch process checks linked behavior; the attacker pays capital per identity and risks losing it, making large-scale Sybil farming costly rather than merely tedious.
